text.tspan: Two promises, not one: the first gives you the response, the second gives you the body.
Headers and status arrive first; the body
is still streaming in. That is why reading
it is a second, separate promise, and why
you can only read the body ONCE.
fetch rejects only on a NETWORK failure.
A 404 or 500 is a successful round trip,
so you must check it yourself:
A different origin means a different
scheme, host or port. The browser sends
the request, but hides the response
The fix is on the SERVER, never in your
None of this blocks the page. fetch hands the work to the browser, your function suspends at the await, and the callback
comes back as a MICROTASK once the response is ready: the same event-loop rule as every other promise.
